abstract: Video acquisition plays a critical role in many scientific experiments, enabling the quantification of human or animal behaviour, and movement of physical systems. Scientific applications place exacting demands on video acquisition, often requiring multiple cameras, high frame rates, synchronisation between cameras or with other hardware, control of camera parameters, and efficient data storage with comprehensive metadata. Here we present pyMultiVideo, an open-source Python application for scientific video acquisition. Features of the software include a graphical user interface (GUI) for efficiently configuring and running multi-camera experiments, online video compression using the computer's GPU, and synchronisation through recording GPIO pins states or external frame triggering. The code-base is simple and modular, with a separation of camera API from GUI code to facilitate adding support for additional camera systems. We outline the design and functionality of the software and present validation experiments demonstrating simultaneous recording and compression from multi-camera setups, at high frame rates without dropped frames on modest computer hardware.
